text:
oliver: heads-up — observed repeated OOMs on gpu-23 during long-context runs (>35k tokens). host shows kv-cache walking into heavy paging and high eviction failures. stack trace attached from the runtime profiler below.

michelle: :eyes: which model / kernel version?

oliver: using rwd-v2-13b quantized, kernel-selector v1.9. logs show sustained KV footprint growth even after request completes. looks like reused prefixes not being reclaimed quickly.

raj: can you paste the profiler excerpt?

oliver: sure:
```
[profile] host_memcpy_ms: 3120
kernel_stall_ms: 1840
kv_evictions_failed: 42
kv_pages_swapped: 1283
avg_kv_alloc_per_request: 24MB
active_prefixes: 97
mean_prefix_lifetime_s: 420
```

amy: hm allocator churn + memcpy cost. long-lived prefixes + small batches amplify duplication in KV sets. batching heuristics may be creating many tiny inflight prefill windows.

dani: did we see any correlation to kernel selection? maybe fallback to different attention kernel increases working set?

oliver: good point — when kernel-selector picks the attention-fused kernel we see lower compute latency but slightly larger temporary KV scratch. In these traces the selector alternated across requests leading to inconsistent KV sizing.

infra-bot: incident created: IN-2026-2309 — OOM storm on gpu-23 (eng-runtime). Pager alerted at 2026-03-12T21:05:34Z.

michelle: immediate mitigation ideas? prefer config flips we can do with low blast radius.

raj: short list: 1) ingress backpressure / fail-fast for requests that request > X history tokens (reject or route to stateless), 2) tighten batch token ceiling so prefill windows don't overlap so much, 3) enable aggressive soft-evict policy to shed cold prefixes sooner.

amy: 2) seems quickest. reduce batch.max_total_tokens from 8192 -> 4096 on Dedicated pool canary. also set kv.soft_evict_threshold=0.75 and kv.evict_scan_target=50 (more frequent pruning).

oliver: drafted a canary patch to change batching heuristics + soft-evict. small config diff below:
```yaml
serve.runtime.batch.max_total_tokens: 4096
serve.runtime.batch.max_inflight_requests: 32
serve.runtime.kv.soft_evict_threshold: 0.75
serve.runtime.kv.evict_scan_target: 50
serve.runtime.kv.allow_spill_to_host: true
```

dani: allow_spill_to_host is riskier latency-wise but will reduce GPU OOM. can we enable for only gpu-23 and a canary instance?

deploy-bot: rolling config canary to gpu-23:deploy-group-a (1/3) — started.

oliver: also adding a lightweight runtime fallback: if kv.alloc_growth_rate > 10MB/s over 30s, mark request as "short-history" and drop prefix cache for that session. saves memory at expense of some quality.

michelle: good. timeline? if canary is green for 30m we can roll to other hosts in the pool. please note in postmortem to measure QoE delta.

raj: followups: 1) add a perf test that simulates 50 concurrent long-context chat sessions to reproduce growth; 2) add kernel-selector telemetry to trace selected kernel per request; 3) experiment with per-prefix reference counting + TTL compaction.

amy: I'll own the perf test. raj can take the selector telemetry. oliver can drive the canary and quick rollback if latency degrades >15% p95.

dani: one more thought — batching heuristics: consider packing by prefix-id when possible so shared prefixes aren't duplicated across batches. might reduce KV duplication. but it's a medium-term change.

oliver: agreed — add as engineering P2. For now, canary in flight. infra-bot: escalate to SEV2 if OOMs resume after config flip.

infra-bot: noted. will notify on recurrence.

michelle: thanks everyone. Please keep thread updated with canary metrics (kv usage, p95 latency, failed-evictions). I'll prep a short comms note for impacted customers if we need wider rollback. :thumbsup:
